subjects.heading: Cryptography
subjects.summary: Methods and systems for confidentiality, integrity, authentication, signatures, trust, key lifecycle, and cryptographic recovery.

includes: Encryption, decryption, hashing, and integrity checks
Digital signatures, certificates, identity, and authentication
Key generation, custody, storage, rotation, backup, and recovery
Application signing, package identity, and cryptographic continuity
Threat models, implementation review, and independent verification
excludes: Authorization to access or change a device, account, key, or repository
Execution of installation, migration, signing, or key-rotation actions without required user approval
Claims that a public certificate or signed artifact reveals or reconstructs its private key

stewardship.responsibility: Cryptographic architecture, system boundaries, trust relationships, and security objectives.
Key identity and lifecycle history, provenance, continuity, backup, and recovery records.
Cryptographic foundations, algorithms, standards, source research, and evidence synthesis.
Clear explanations, user dialogue, coordination, and communication between technical roles.
Implementation, application signing, secure-storage integration, and reproducible tests.
Security requirements, key custody, permissions, threat boundaries, and integrity constraints.
Adversarial review, failure cases, alternatives, weaknesses, and recovery options.
Cross-component integration, dependency analysis, and reconciliation that preserves source disagreements.
Independent verification of claims, certificates, signatures, implementation, and acceptance criteria.

subheadings.heading: Foundations, algorithms, and standards
subheadings.description: Mathematical foundations, algorithm families, protocol standards, security properties, and current research.

subheadings.heading: Cryptographic architecture and trust boundaries
subheadings.description: System design, trust assumptions, component boundaries, threat surfaces, and cryptographic dependencies.

subheadings.heading: Encryption and decryption
subheadings.description: Confidentiality mechanisms, key agreement, encryption modes, protocol use, and safe implementation constraints.

subheadings.heading: Hashing and integrity
subheadings.description: Cryptographic hashes, message authentication, checksums, integrity manifests, and verification boundaries.

subheadings.heading: Digital signatures and certificates
subheadings.description: Signing and verification, certificate identity, trust chains, algorithms, and signature evidence.

subheadings.heading: Key generation, custody, and rotation
subheadings.description: Key creation, entropy, custody, access controls, rotation, revocation, and lifecycle accountability.

subheadings.heading: Identity, trust, and authentication
subheadings.description: Identity binding, authentication protocols, trust establishment, certificate validation, and impersonation resistance.

subheadings.heading: Android application signing and package continuity
subheadings.description: APK signing identities, signing certificates, package update compatibility, build provenance, and migration safety.

subheadings.heading: Secure storage, backup, and recovery
subheadings.description: Keystore-backed storage, protected backups, recovery plans, key-loss boundaries, and reversible migration design.

subheadings.heading: Threat models and adversarial review
subheadings.description: Attack surfaces, abuse cases, compromise scenarios, implementation weaknesses, and alternative defenses.

subheadings.heading: Integration and reconciliation
subheadings.description: Dependencies across applications, devices, services, build systems, identity records, and recovery workflows.

subheadings.heading: Independent verification
subheadings.description: Independent signature checks, certificate fingerprints, reproducibility, test evidence, and acceptance review.

subheadings.heading: Explanation and coordination
subheadings.description: User-facing explanations, question routing, terminology, communication, and explicit handoffs.
